content.title: ASU rankings | Arizona State University
content.text: Home About ASU ASU rankings Repeatedly ranked #1 Recognized globally as a leading knowledge enterprise, Arizona State University is dedicated to delivering academic excellence, advancing research-based solutions for humankind’s greatest challenges, producing strong and compassionate leaders, ensuring the health of our planet and providing quality education for all learners. View all of ASU's No. 1 rankings. ASU has topped U.S. News & World Report’s “Most Innovative Schools” list since the inception of the category in 2016. ASU again placed ahead of MIT and Stanford, based on a survey of peers. College presidents, provosts and admissions deans around the country nominated up to 15 colleges or universities that are making the most innovative improvements. Read more Ahead of MIT and Stanford ASU is ranked No. 1 in the nation — ahead of MIT and Penn State — and top 10 in the world six years in a row by Times Higher Education for advancing the United Nations' 17 Sustainable Development Goals. ASU ranks No. 1 in the U.S. for 11 of 17 (60%) of categories used to measure global impact. ASU is the only U.S. university ranked in the top 50 worldwide out of approximately 2,500 institutions.Read more Ahead of MIT and Penn State ASU ranks No. 2 in the U.S. among public universities, for the fourth straight year, in the GEURS survey of employers. GEURS rates employability performance on key employability drivers: specialization, graduate skills, academic performance, focus on work expertise, social impact and leadership, and internationality.Read more Ahead of UCLA, University of Michigan and Purdue Scoring a perfect 100/100 for the fourth year in a row, the Thunderbird School of Global Management is ranked No. 1 in the world for international trade by the QS International Trade Rankings, ahead of Cambridge, Oxford and Columbia. QS selected Thunderbird’s Master of Global Management degree program as the world’s best international trade program.Read more Ahead of Cambridge, Oxford and Columbia The Broadcast Education Association awarded the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communications a #1 ranking for top-winning news programs. Cronkite students' work was honored with 14 undergraduate awards and five graduate awards at the BEA's Festival of Media Arts competition.Read more Ahead of Syracuse, Florida and USC ASU is ranked No. 5 among U.S. public universities for undergraduate teaching by U.S. News & World Report, ahead of UCLA, Purdue and Wisconsin. This award recognizes universities demonstrating a strong commitment to high-quality undergraduate teaching.Read more Ahead of UCLA, Purdue and Wisconsin W. P. Carey School of Business ranks among the top in the nation with six of its online graduate programs in the top 10 — including online MBA (top 10 for 13 consecutive years), general management MBA, MBA marketing, MBA business analytics, finance MBA and master's in business programs (excluding MBA).Read more W. P. Carey programs rank in the top 10 ASU ranks No. 1 in the U.S. and No. 2 in the world by the Association for the Advancement of Sustainability in Higher Education, earning 91.10 points out of 100. With more than 1,200 participants in 52 countries, the index placed ASU in the top 10 worldwide for six “impact areas" including energy and climate, doctoral and research institutions, transportation, research, procurement and waste and investment.Read more Ahead of Stanford and UC Berkeley ASU is ranked No. 3 in the U.S. among public universities for first-year experiences, ahead of Michigan, Purdue and Wisconsin, by U.S. News & World Report. First-year students have access to unique programs that help them thrive including peer coaching, an interactive chatbot and Welcome Week activities.Read more Ahead of Michigan, Purdue and Wisconsin Recognized for preparing students to make an impact in the digital economy, ASU ranks No. 4 in the U.S. among public universities for overall digital leadership by the Digital Leaders in Higher Education survey. Based on employer evaluations and career outcomes, the ranking measures impact in digital transformation management; computer science; digital entrepreneurship; and data science, AI and business analytics. Read more Ahead of UCLA, Purdue and University of Arizona ASU is ranked the top public university in the U.S. chosen by international students, for the fifth straight year, in the 2025 Institute of International Education Open Doors Report. Placing ahead of University of Illinois, Purdue and UC Berkeley, ASU hosted over 20,368 international students in the 2024–25 academic year.Read more Ahead of Illinois, Purdue and UC Berkeley Washington Monthly places ASU top 10 in the U.S. among public universities in its 2025 Best Colleges for Your Tuition (and Tax) Dollars ranking, ahead of UCLA, Wisconsin and Illinois. More than 1,400 institutions were ranked in four categories for their contribution to public good: access, affordability, outcomes and promoting community and national service.Read more Ahead of UCLA, Wisconsin and Illinois ASU is one of 21 R1 universities recognized in new Carnegie classification for broad student access and high earnings and one of only three universities in the U.S. that is also a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities.Read more ASU outperforms Ohio State and Penn State ASU has been named a top 20 "Best College for Future Leaders" among public universities by TIME and Statista. The ranking is based on the career milestones of a selected group of the nation's top leaders in the U.S. including where they received their degrees. The list of leaders spans a broad range of industries and fields, including politicians, CEOs, union leaders and Nobel winners. ASU has been named to the Mental Health Services Honor Roll by The Princeton Review. Universities were selected for staffing and student support, healthy campus quality of life, and empowerment of students to address mental health through programs and peer-to-peer offerings.Read more Along with Princeton, MIT and Columbia Recognized for preparing students to make an impact in the digital economy, ASU ranks No. 3 among public universities for online digital leadership by the Digital Leaders in Higher Education survey. Based on employer evaluations and career outcomes, the ranking measures impact in digital transformation management; computer science; digital entrepreneurship; and data science, AI and business analytics.Read more Ahead of Washington, Texas and Purdue ASU's undergraduate chemistry program ranks in the top 20 in Washington Monthly's America's Top Colleges for Women in STEM, along with Carnegie Mellon and the University of Buffalo. Based on data from the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System, the ranking compared the gender distribution of every STEM program at 1,027 U.S. colleges and universities. ASU ranks top 40 among U.S. universities according to QS World University Rankings 2026, ahead of Dartmouth, Georgetown and Notre Dame. Moving up two spots from last year's position, ASU takes the top spot in the state. QS looked at key indicators including academic reputation, sustainability, employment outcomes and international research network.Read more Ahead of Dartmouth, Georgetown and Notre Dame ASU ranks among the nation's 25 Best-in-Class Colleges. According to Washington Monthly, ASU is "affordable, flexible, career focused and rich in opportunity. ... And as a model for what large public universities might become — open-access, innovation driven and public spirited — it remains one of the most important institutions in American higher education."Read more Along with Princeton, Johns Hopkins and UC Berkeley ASU ranks No. 1 in engineering and non-science research expenditures by the National Science Foundation’s Higher Education Research and Development survey, surpassing $1 billion in annual research funding in 2024. Leading the way in technological innovation, ASU researchers are using AI to improve health care globally by helping doctors detect problems earlier and personalize care.Read more Ahead of Penn, Harvard and Wisconsin ASU ranks top 15 in the nation for its executive MBA program by Financial Times Business Research. The ranking demonstrates ASU's widespread impact through its emphasis on business knowledge and research in addressing problems on a global scale. In the U.S. News & World Report's 2025 graduate rankings, ASU's local government management graduate program ranks No. 3 in the country, ahead of Syracuse University, Indiana and Georgia. It is one of seven graduate program specialties offered in ASU's Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions ranked in the top 10.Read more Ahead of Syracuse, Indiana and Georgia ASU is top 15 in the U.S. for producing Fulbright students and ranks third among U.S. public doctoral-granting universities. The Fulbright Program provides opportunities for exceptional students to study, teach and conduct research through international exchange and collaboration. ASU has been a "top-producing institution" for the Fulbright U.S. Student Program for 20 of the past 22 years.Read more Ahead of Stanford, USC and Johns Hopkins ASU ranks No. 5 among U.S. public universities for best co-op and internship programs by U.S. News & World Report. College presidents, provosts and admissions deans from more than 1,500 schools nominated institutions that require or encourage students to apply what they're learning in real-world circumstances through internships, practicums or cooperative education. Read more Along with Georgia Tech, Purdue and Clemson The Broadcast Education Association awarded the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communications a #2 overall ranking for Institutional Excellence in Media, along with top five honors in multiple media categories. Cronkite students' work was honored with 14 undergraduate awards and five graduate awards at the BEA's Festival of Media Arts competition.Read more Ahead of Syracuse, Florida and USC ASU is among the top 5 for best online education master's programs by U.S. News & World Report, 2026. Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation has four online master's programs in the top 5, including educational and instructional media (#1), curriculum and instruction (#2), educational administration (#4) and special education (#4). Read more Graduate programs among the nation’s best The Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions ranks No. 2 for best graduate homeland security and emergency management program by the 2025 U.S. News & World Report, ahead of USC, George Washington and Columbia.Read more Ahead of USC, George Washington and Columbia ASU ranks No. 2 in the Energy and Climate category by the Association for the Advancement of Sustainability in Higher Education in its annual Sustainable Campus Index report. The ranking recognizes ASU for helping to mitigate climate change impacts by reducing its greenhouse gas emissions, phasing out fossil fuels and investing in clean, renewable energy.Read more Ahead of Stanford, UC Santa Barbara and Yale ASU is among the top 20 public universities on Times Higher Education's Most International Universities in the World 2024 list. The ranking recognizes universities that have a high proportion of international students and staff, collaborate with researchers worldwide, and have a strong global reputation. ASU ranks top 10 in the nation and No. 14 globally for interdisciplinary science by Times Higher Education, ahead of Michigan, Illinois and Texas. The ranking evaluates more than 600 universities worldwide in three areas: financial investment, institutional support and research output.Read more Ahead of Michigan, Illinois and Texas ASU recorded an average multiyear Academic Progress Rate of 995 over a four-year period (2018–19 to 2021–22), which ties the all-time ASU high and first in the Pac-12 for the second year in a row. Since the 2015–16 academic year, ASU has averaged a 990-plus for each APR multiyear cohort that has been released. Read more Sun Devil Athletics matches average multiyear APR high W. P. Carey School of Business ranks No. 5 in the U.S. and No. 8 worldwide in Poets & Quants 2026 rankings of MBA entrepreneurship programs. Measuring10 categories, the ranking measures student entrepreneurship while emphasizing supportive ecosystems and mentor engagement. ASU is among the top 5 for best online engineering master's programs by U.S. News & World Report, 2026. Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering's has 3 online master's programs in the top 5, including engineering management, electrical engineering and industrial engineering. Read more Graduate programs among the nation’s best ASU's W. P. Carey School of Business offers 27 degree programs, both undergraduate and graduate and including online, that rank among the country's top 25, and 11 in the top 10. Top programs include supply chain management, project management, information systems and business analytics.Read more 27 top-ranked degree programs ASU's Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation ranks No. 15 in U.S. News & World Report's annual rankings of America's best graduate education programs. The college placed ahead of Michigan State, Washington and Illinois, solidifying ASU as a top-tier college for a master's degree in education since 2012.Read more Ahead of Michigan State, Washington and Illinois The annual QS World University Rankings recognizes ASU as a top 10 university in the world for the quality of meaningful connections between potential employers and students — ahead of Princeton, MIT and Stanford, and others. ASU also earns the No. 17 ranking for the excellence of its partnerships with employers — ahead of Cornell, UCLA, Princeton and Harvard.Read more Ahead of Princeton, MIT and Stanford ASU is named to the top 100 in the world for academic reputation by Times Higher Education. The ranking is based on the world's largest invitation-only academic opinion survey, which uses United Nations data as a guide to ensure that the results are representative of world scholarship, and targets only experienced, published scholars. Read more Top 100 worldwide for academic reputation For the past ten years, ASU has been one of the top producers of Teach for America corps members — a trend that continued in 2025 with ASU ranking No. 2 among large universities, ahead of UCLA, UC Berkeley and Illinois. TFA corps members spend two years in classrooms supporting the educational and personal development of underserved students.Read more Ahead of UCLA, UC Berkeley and Illinois ASU ranks in the top 10 in the U.S. for NASA-funded higher education R&D expenditures in the National Science Foundation Higher Education Research and Development survey, surpassing $1 billion in annual research funding in 2024. A notable deep-space study, the Psyche mission, launched to explore a metal-rich asteroid and could offer unique insights into Earth's core.Read more Ahead of MIT, UCLA, Michigan and Stanford The Princeton Review ranks ASU a top U.S. university for undergraduate education in its "The Best 388 Colleges 2023" based on a survey of more than 160,000 students. Students praised the university for "innovation," the ability to “personalize every student’s experience,” "endless ... opportunities for success" and "diversity" of the student body. Read more Princeton Review ranks ASU among “Best Colleges” ASU ranks in the top 5 among universities without a medical school for inventions, patents, patent deals and startups by AUTM, ahead of Georgia Tech, UC Berkeley and Princeton. ASU is one of only two of 63 universities without medical schools, including MIT to rank in the top five across all four categories.Read more Ahead of Georgia Tech, UC Berkeley and Princeton ASU ranks No. 8 among top-tier research universities on The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression’s 2024 College Free Speech Rankings, ahead of University of Chicago, Duke and Purdue. The ranking is based on student responses, school's approach toward free expression concerning incoming speakers and school policies that imperil free speech. Read more Ahead of University of Chicago, Duke and Purdue For the second time, ASU has earned the Seal of Excelencia from the Washington, D.C.-based organization Excelencia in Education for its high level of commitment and effort to serve Latino students. In 2019, ASU was among the inaugural group of nine institutions to earn the prestigious award. Read more Seal of Excelencia for support of Latino students ASU earns the "Education Partner of the Year" award from the Hispanic Scholarship Fund, recognizing the university's efforts to help more Hispanic students attend and graduate from college. ASU's undergraduate Hispanic student enrollment has grown 29% over the past six years. In addition, ASU is currently home to 225 HSF Scholars, receiving mentorship, career support and leadership development. Read more Recognized for service to Hispanic students and families Times Higher Education recognizes ASU as one of only two universities in the U.S. — and one of 31 globally — to achieve net zero emissions. The ranking appears in THE’s new data-led report on higher education’s climate-neutral commitments, The Race to Net Zero, which shows how universities worldwide are lowering their greenhouse gas emissions to achieve net zero.Read more Along with American University ASU ranks No. 1 in anthropology research expenditures by the National Science Foundation’s Higher Education Research and Development survey, surpassing $1 billion in annual research funding in 2024. In a major study, ASU anthropologists created a database of Sonoran Desert Huhugam archaeology, enabling researchers across the globe to access the information.Read more Ahead of Michigan, Harvard and Duke ASU ranks No. 8 among U.S. public universities for best learning communities by U.S. News & World Report. College presidents, provosts and admissions deans from more than 1,500 schools nominated up to 15 institutions with stellar examples of stellar learning communities. Schools that received 10 or more nominations were ranked.Read more Along with Virginia Tech and Florida State ASU is named among seven "Greenest College Campuses in the U.S." by Newsweek, along with Stanford, Cornell and University of Colorado Boulder. The ranking recognizes universities whose emphasis on sustainability reflects the mindset of the majority of young people who, according to an international Lancet study, are concerned about climate change. ASU ranks top 25 worldwide by ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects in eight subject areas, including No. 14 in environmental science and engineering and No. 18 in geography. ASU ranks top 25 in the U.S. in 20 subject areas. ASU ranks top 10 among universities worldwide granted U.S. utility patents in the top 100 rankings by the National Academy of Inventors for the third consecutive year. ASU placed No. 5 among U.S. universities and No. 9 worldwide, demonstrating its dedication to propelling American technological advancement. ASU has ranked in the top 10 five times since 2018.Read more Along with MIT, Stanford and Michigan ASU ranks in the top 1% of international universities for education, employability, faculty and research among more than 21,000 universities by the Center for World University Rankings, ahead of Notre Dame and Georgetown. Over 21,000 universities were ranked by the Center of World University Rankings. Recognizing ASU for “improving teaching and learning, producing research that makes a difference in communities and revitalizing its civic and academic mission," the Carnegie Foundation bestows its "Community Engagement" classification on the university through 2025. Read more A distinctive classification through 2025 ASU makes Newsweek's list of The Best Maker Schools in Higher Education, among more than 2,000 communal makerspaces around the world. The list was created through a survey tool in collaboration with an international community of educators, administrators, students and maker leaders. The selected schools demonstrate the ingenuity and community engagement that are hallmarks of the maker movement. ASU graduate programs place among the best in the nation, according to U.S. News & World Report's 2025 “Best Graduate Schools” rankings. Nineteen graduate programs rank among the top 10 including homeland security and emergency management, supply chain and nonprofit management, and information and technology management.Read more 19 programs rank among the top 10 nationwide ASU is No. 15 on the Peace Corps 2025 list of top volunteer-producing colleges and universities, ahead of UCLA, Indiana and Ohio State. Sun Devil volunteers make a difference through meaningful service in more than 70 countries, developing cross-cultural, leadership, language, teaching and community development skills. ASU's Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law is among the nation's top 20 public university graduate schools according to U.S. News & World Report. With four specialty programs in the top 20 and the legal writing program ranked third in the nation, the ranking marks the 16th consecutive year the college earned this distinction.Read more Ahead of Indiana University, Washington and University of Arizona ASU continues to set the standard in online learning, earning a gold rating in the inaugural Times Higher Education Online Learning Rankings. ASU was one of only 11 global universities that received gold designation, the highest recognition for quality.Read more ASU sets the standard in online learning For the third consecutive year, ASU is named as a Fulbright HSI (Hispanic-Serving Institution) Leader by the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. The accolade recognizes the university's service to the Hispanic community and placement of faculty and students into the prestigious Fulbright program. The Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions at ASU ranks No. 2 for best graduate criminology and criminal justice programs by U.S. News & World Report, ahead of Penn State and Florida State. One of 14 graduate degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationwide, the program is designed and taught by nationally ranked faculty.Read more Ahead of Penn State and Florida State For the past 10 years, ASU has been a top producer of elite scholars. The list includes, among others, 335 Gilman Scholars, 169 Fulbright U.S. Student Program participants, 49 DAAD-Rise recipients, 41 Boren Scholars, 28 Killiam Fellows, 21 Goldwater Scholars, 28 CLS Scholars, 10 Udall Scholars, 10 Pickering Scholars, 6 Gates Cambridge Scholars and 3 Rhodes Scholars.Read more Elite national scholars ASU's Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law has four programs ranked in the top 20, including No. 3 for its legal writing program, by U.S. News & World Report. Preparing law students with the writing and analytical skills essential for success in legal practice, the legal writing program has consistently ranked in the top 10 for 16 consecutive years.Read more Ahead of University of Arizona, Duke and Texas A&M ASU's School of Public Affairs holds eight top 10 spots in U.S. News & World Report graduate rankings, including the school itself, along with several specialties such as homeland security and emergency management, information and technology management, local government management, nonprofit management, public management and leadership, urban policy and criminology.Read more Highly ranked in several specialties ASU is ranked No. 2 for visual and performing arts by the National Science Foundation Survey of Earned Doctorates, ahead of UCLA, Columbia and Yale.The SED is based on the number and characteristics of individuals receiving research doctoral degrees in the academic year 2023–24 from U.S. academic institutions.Read more Ahead of UCLA, Columbia and Yale ASU ranks in the nation's top 15 public schools by Washington Monthly's 2023 National University Rankings, ahead of University of Virginia, UC Santa Barbara and Ohio State. The ranking recognizes colleges' contribution to the public good in three categories: social mobility, research and promoting public service. Read more Ahead of University of Virginia, UC Santa Barbara and Ohio State ASU's W. P. Carey School of Business has been named one of the nation's most outstanding business schools, according to the Princeton Review. The W. P. Carey School earned the No. 1 spot in the country for Best MBA for operations, the No. 5 spot in resources for minority students, and No. 11 for online MBA programs.Read more W. P. Carey School of Business named an outstanding business school ASU ranks #18 in the U.S. among public universities in the National Science Foundation Survey of Earned Doctorates. The SED is based on the number and characteristics of individuals receiving research doctoral degrees. ASU was in the top 20 Institutions for five subjects, including engineering, social sciences and humanities. More than 60,000 employers and partners from the Global University Central Career Union and Lockin selected ASU as a recipient of its Top 50 Professional Collaboration Support Global University Award. The award recognizes outstanding participation in recruitment activities, collaboration with Chinese enterprises, helping their students to seek employment and improving their employment rate. ASU ranks top 5 nationally for research expenditures among universities without a medical school, according to the National Science Foundation HERD survey, surpassing $1 billion in research funding. Advancing high-impact research, ASU scientists have built a powerful processor to improve space communications for national defense.The data for this ranking was measured prior to the launching of ASU's John Shufeldt School of Medicine and Medical Engineering, set to open in fall 2026.Read more Ahead of University of Colorado-Boulder, Purdue and Princeton ASU's Army Reserve Officers' Training Corps, also known as ROTC, is recognized as one of the top eight programs of its kind nationwide with the 2021 General Douglas MacArthur Award. Chosen out of 274, the program known as the Sun Devil Battalion was selected for a combination of achievement in commissioning mission, cadets' performance during Cadet Summer Training and retention rates. Read more Top-ranked ROTC program
